summary.intent: Design and implement three related memory-loop features: memory editing (title/body/keywords), keyword-based injection boosting, and a configurable generation threshold system with named presets.
summary.outcome: A fully implemented and committed feature set across 14 tasks covering CLI subcommands, TUI wizard edits, injection scoring, generator filtering, and settings persistence — all tests passing including canary E2E.

repo: MemoryRecord reconciliation preserves user keywords by omission — fields not explicitly copied during ReconcileGeneratedRecords are naturally preserved.
Mode and ActivationPolicy are stored on the memoryloop Store (memory-loop.json), not settings.json — threshold was added to Store for consistency so TUI can read from one source.
The wrapcheck linter requires fmt.Errorf wrapping on errors returned from CLI command functions in memory_loop_cmd.go.
confidenceRank already returns ordered integers (low=1, medium=2, high=3) in generator.go, enabling threshold comparison via < instead of == equality checks.
The memorylooptui settings tab reads from m.state.Store, not settings.json directly — threshold fields needed to be added to the Store struct to be accessible in the TUI.
mise lint gates on errcheck, gosec, goconst, wrapcheck, ireturn, and revive — must run after every substantive change.

code.finding: confidenceLow rejection gate uses == equality; the new threshold system converts this to confidenceRank comparison for configurable minimum confidence.
confidenceRank function returns low=1, medium=2, high=3 — used to implement ordered threshold comparisons.
GenerateInput is constructed here during refresh; threshold config is injected at this point from resolved settings.
memoryCfg was declared twice after threshold wiring — caused a redeclaration compile error that required removing the duplicate.

workflow: Adversarial/Codex review run twice on the spec surfaced real design flaws (multi-word keyword tokenization, missing $EDITOR failure modes, singleton policy bool vs tri-state) before implementation began.
The Codex companion script hit ENOBUFS buffer overflow when run against a large working tree with binary/DB files — falling back to a subagent review was an effective workaround.
Running mise lint after Task 14 (not after each task) resulted in 3 wrapcheck lint failures that needed fixing in a separate pass — per feedback, lint should run after each task.
Subagents leave changes staged/unstaged; only the orchestrator commits — confirmed by user correction mid-session.
Self-review checklist (placeholder scan, internal consistency, spec coverage) caught a missing parseKeywords() helper in the Files Changed table before the plan was finalized.

friction: Codex companion script (codex-companion.mjs) failed with ENOBUFS when run against a large working tree containing binary files (insights.db) — had to fall back to a subagent-based adversarial review.
Three wrapcheck lint errors in memory_loop_cmd.go appeared only after Task 14's lint pass — should have been caught per-task.
memoryCfg redeclaration compile error introduced during Task 13 threshold wiring required a manual fix.
The TUI settings tab reads from Store not settings.json, which created an architectural mismatch since the spec placed threshold in settings.json — resolved by adding threshold fields to Store.
The user repeated 'spec written to docs/...' twice without providing feedback, causing a brief ambiguous exchange before moving on.
open_items: Keywords on generated memories create a reconciliation trap when a user edits a generated memory (changing its fingerprint) and the generator later produces an updated version — both versions can coexist; spec documents this but no automated resolution.
SIGINT during $EDITOR session can leave a stale temp file — spec notes this as a known pattern (same as git commit) but no cleanup code was specified.
CLI edit subcommand interactive mode (no flags = huh prompts) is standalone huh forms, not the full TUI app — this divergence in UX is intentional but may confuse users.

Score visibility in the injection prompt tester (showing per-memory keyword match counts) was noted as a spec gap but handled implicitly via the existing reason field — no explicit score breakdown UI was added.
Overlapping phrase keywords (e.g., 'go' and 'go test' both present) each match independently — cumulative boosting behavior is documented but not capped.
